title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency and throughput benchmarks vs their baseline provider. Covered p95/p99 latencies across token lengths, batching/KV cache tuning, quantization tradeoffs, and plan for an end-to-end load run. Agreed on next steps: share full benchmark spreadsheet, run region-specific test, and schedule canary rollout. Customer asked for security docs and rough pricing estimate for Dedicated capacity.

Customer to provide production sample prompt set and region for E2E test - Priya - due 2025-08-21
Schedule canary rollout planning call w/infra (Maya) - 2025-08-26

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (HelioHealth ML), Carlos Reyes (HelioHealth Platform), Lori Matthews (Product), Zoe Kim (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio/vid OK?
[00:08] Priya: Yep, good here.
[00:10] Maya: Cool. Agenda - quick run through of last week's tuning changes, then benchmark numbers comparing Redwood vs their baseline, and then next steps for the E2E load. Ethan, you wanna kick off with the numbers?
[00:20] Ethan: Sure. So we ran the bench on the same 512-token prompt set you provided last week. I have p95 and p99 across three batch configurations - single request, auto-batch 4, and auto-batch 8. For reference, baseline provider numbers were from Helio's supplied runs on BaselineCloud.
[00:34] Ethan: High level - Redwood p95 for 512 tokens at our recommended config (batch=4, kv cache enabled) is ~120 ms median for the generation portion, end-to-end average is about 180 ms. Baseline p95 we saw around 220 ms, end-to-end ~320 ms. p99 for Redwood is ~320 ms vs baseline ~650 ms. So we're roughly 1.8-2x better on tail latency in these runs.
[01:02] Carlos: Sorry can you repeat the p95 numbers for single-request mode? We mostly do single-request low-latency for our UI.
[01:08] Ethan: Right, single-request (no batching) p95 was 150 ms for the model step, end-to-end 230 ms. Baseline single-request was 290 ms p95. So even without batching we're seeing a big delta.
[01:22] Priya: Those numbers look promising, but curious — what's the token/sec throughput at batch sizes? Our peak load is about 10k tokens/sec per region during daytime.
[01:32] Ethan: At batch=4 we measured ~5,200 tokens/sec sustained on the instance type we used. Batch=8 pushes to ~7,500 tokens/sec but adds a small median latency bump (~20-30 ms). Baseline at batch=4 was ~3,300 tokens/sec in their published runs.
[01:48] Lori: Are those test instances comparable? Like same GPU type? I want to make sure apples-to-apples.
[01:53] Ethan: Good question. We used A100-80GB equivalent on our side (we run on the customer-dedicated config for tests), and the baseline ran on V100-class in their notes — they didn't disclose exact kernel variants. There's some mismatch, but we also ran a matched-hardware test where we spun up an A100 baseline and still saw Redwood advantage ~1.5x on throughput.
[02:14] Zoe: From security perspective we need the raw logs and the instrumentation to validate no customer data persisted in the run. Can you include that?
[02:22] Maya: Absolutely — Ethan will share the CSVs and the log export, and we'll redact identifiable tokens per your request.
[02:29] Ethan: Yep, I'll include request IDs, timestamps and stage timings (serialize, model, postprocess). Quick caveat: transcription of stage names may be slightly different in the exported sheets, e.g., "kv-cache" shows as "K V cache" in one of our older integration exports.
[02:44] Priya: Haha yeah I noticed that in the sample. Not a blocker.
[02:47] Ethan: On tuning — enabling prefix/KV cache helped p95 by ~20-25% for repeated prompts, batching helped throughput. We also tested int8 quantized variant which reduced GPU memory by ~30% and improved throughput by ~15% but added ~10-15 ms median latency; p99 variance nudged up a bit. So tradeoff exists between cost and tail latency.
[03:12] Priya: Is the quantized model only available on Dedicated or can we test it on the hosted env for the pilot?
[03:18] Ethan: Quantization works in both, but for the pilot we recommend Dedicated pools for consistent performance; hosted has variable noisy neighbors. That said we can open a trial Dedicated slot for you for a week if you want to validate.
[03:30] Carlos: For the UI path we care about p99 more than median. You mentioned p99 improved but still had variance — what caused the tail spikes?
[03:38] Ethan: Two main causes: cold KV cache misses and occasional kernel scheduling delays when batch join thresholds spike. We mitigated by setting a soft batch timeout and reserving a small number of pre-warmed slots. Also routing by latency SLO helps keep high-priority traffic on lower-occupancy instances.
[03:56] Priya: What's the recommended soft batch timeout? We tried 50 ms previously and saw latency jump.
[04:01] Ethan: For your workload we recommend 15-25 ms. We used 20 ms in these runs which gave a good balance — throughput gains while keeping p95 low.
[04:09] Lori: Can you remind me of the fallback behavior — if Dedicated is saturated, we can route to hosted or lower-cost model?
[04:15] Maya: Yep — our routing policies support fallback to compatible model variants or regions. You can set canary rollouts, automatic fallback to a smaller quantized instance, or route to hosted with a flag. We'll send the routing policy doc.
[04:27] Zoe: KMS and data residency — do you have a checklist for what Redwood needs to integrate with our KMS and VPC peering?
[04:34] Maya: Yes — we'll attach the KMS integration guide and VPC peering checklist. Also include our SOC2 report and penetration test summary.
[04:42] Ethan: Back to benchmarks — we also ran a long-run 30-minute sustained load at your peak token/sec and saw memory pressure around the 27th minute on the baseline node, causing retries and increased p99. Our setup hit steady-state without retries.
[04:58] Carlos: So in practice that means fewer retries and better UX for users during peaks. Good.
[05:02] Priya: For billing and cost, how does this translate? If Redwood is faster but uses slightly larger instances with Dedicated, are we still likely to save?
[05:11] Maya: Short answer — yes in most cases. Because you pay per-slot and per-token, lower latency and higher throughput reduce per-token GPU cycles. Our Optimize toolkit gave an example showing 20-30% unit-cost improvement vs baseline when using recommended batching and caching. Ethan will run a specific cost estimate for your sample load.
[05:29] Ethan: I'll produce a cost-per-1M-tokens estimate across three configs: hosted, dedicated single-slot, and dedicated scaled pool. I'll include quantized variants.
[05:37] Lori: Great. For the E2E run you mentioned region-specific tests, can we do us-west-2 and eu-west-1?
[05:44] Ethan: Yes, we can run both. For eu-west-1 latencies were ~10-15 ms higher due to region TTL, but throughput was consistent. We'll include both in the spreadsheet.
[05:54] Priya: One small ask — can you share the exact test harness script? I'd like to reproduce locally.
[05:59] Ethan: Sure, we'll attach the harness (curl-based driver + node runner). Note there are a few instrument names that are slightly different in older drivers, but we'll annotate.
[06:10] Zoe: Also we'll need a summary paragraph for procurement stating SLA expectations and fallback guarantees for the pilot.
[06:16] Maya: We'll draft that and send as part of the pricing/engagement note.
[06:21] Carlos: Timeline - if we get the spreadsheet and the E2E run in the next week, we can make a decision by end of month. Is that realistic?
[06:29] Maya: Yes — we can run the region tests and share artifacts by Friday. Then schedule the canary planning call the following Tuesday.
[06:35] Priya: OK sounds good.
[06:37] Ethan: Quick gotcha - in one of the baseline runs their client-side batching caused coalescing that inflated latency numbers; we removed that from the comparison but noted it in the sheet.
[06:48] Priya: Appreciate the transparency.
[06:50] Maya: Any other questions?
[06:52] Lori: Nothing from product.
[06:54] Zoe: No, but will follow up on SOC2 details.
[06:56] Maya: Great. To recap: Ethan shares full benchmark spreadsheet + raw logs + test harness by 2025-08-22; Priya sends final prompt set and region by 2025-08-21; Maya sends pricing estimate and routing doc by 2025-08-24 and schedule canary meeting for 2025-08-26.
[07:15] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:17] Maya: Thanks everyone, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and minor transcription artifacts (e.g., 'K V cache' vs 'KV cache'), timestamps approximate every 10-60s per speaker turn.
